items.title: PM says Australia has 'ideological disagreement' with US after it reveals anti-slavery tariff
items.description: The planned new tariff is to be slapped on dozens of countries that have allegedly failed to take action to prevent slavery and forced labour.

items.title: Live: Greens 'concerned' about Chalmers's tax change powers
items.description: The Greens have raised concerns about the ministerial discretion contained in the federal government's budget bill before parliament. Follow live.

items.title: Paedophile ex-magistrate Peter Liddy leaves prison after 25 years
items.description: Notorious paedophile ex-magistrate Peter Liddy has taken his first steps of freedom after serving a 25-year prison term for the sexual abuse of four children.

items.title: US House votes to rein in Trump on Iran war
items.description: The US House of Representatives delivers President Donald Trump a rare rebuke, voting to halt military action in his war with Iran.

items.title: Pentagon hires convicted January 6 rioter for national security job
items.description: The Trump administration has given a man who was jailed for his actions during the January 6, 2021, US Capitol riot a job in the Pentagon's policy office.

items.title: In a town where a baby died at a homeless campsite, charities say the data does not add up
items.description: As governments work to meet the growing need for social housing, community groups are stepping up to meet the rapidly increasing demand for their services to help fill the gap.

items.title: Boxing trainer suspended after neo-Nazi Sewell trained at his gym
items.description: ABC NEWS Verify can reveal that neo-Nazi Thomas Sewell has been training at a boxing gym in the outer-Melbourne suburb of Diamond Creek, a short drive from where he is living. The gym has been suspended by the sport's governing body.

items.title: ASIO warns Chinese spies using LinkedIn to pry information from applicants
items.description: Australia and its partners in the Five Eyes intelligence alliance warn that Chinese spies are using job platforms to post fake ads to lure recruits with access to sensitive information.

items.title: What's got the Pope and most Australians worried? This hyped new AI technology
items.description: Most Australians appear to distrust and dislike artificial intelligence despite using technology more than people in other countries.

items.title: MP uses parliament to reveal threats to NZYQ deportees in Nauru
items.description: A cohort of refugees deported to Nauru by the federal government have faced threats of violence and verbal abuse, independent MP Andrew Wilkie has revealed under parliamentary privilege.

items.title: Live: ASX falls on renewed Middle East tensions while SpaceX locked for IPO
items.description: The ASX has fallen by more than 1 per cent following Wall Street slipping overnight as hopes for a swift end to the war in Iran faded again. Follow the latest on our live markets blog.

items.title: 'Not enough' bees for crop pollination as parasite takes over
items.description: A new report warns of a massive pollination shortfall in Australia this year as varroa mite wipes out hives and forces beekeepers out.

items.title: Israel and Lebanon renew ceasefire but Hezbollah not present at talks
items.description: Lebanon and Israel have agreed to a ceasefire, according to a joint statement with the United States.

items.title: Neo-Nazi hecklers found guilty over Anzac Day booing
items.description: Three white supremacists who loudly booed during a Welcome to Country ceremony at an Anzac Day dawn service in Melbourne have been found guilty of offensive behaviour and ordered to pay fines.

items.title: What happens when a Restoration Australia project takes five years
items.description: A planned 12-month build that's still underway three years later is the running joke of design shows. But what happens when you're a TV producer trying to make a series of it?

items.title: How to move forward from estrangement
items.description: Experts say healing might involve reducing emotional distress and gaining clarity from the situation.

items.title: Quiz: Can you recognise these 10 classic Australian album covers?
items.description: Take a closer look at some of the biggest albums in Australian music and tell us what you see.

items.title: World number one gutted after 'dirty' loss in French Open quarterfinal
items.description: Aryna Sabalenka feels the pain of a shock loss in the quarterfinals of the French Open, saying she just feels like smashing things.

items.title: Cost-of-living pressure 'entrenching disadvantage' in the NT
items.description: The NT has the second highest average rent in the country, with households having to set aside more of their weekly wages to cover essential costs.

items.title: Australia's economic slowdown is just beginning, experts warn
items.description: The economy grew just 0.3 per cent in the first quarter, gross domestic product per capita went backwards, and interest rate rises and cost-of-living pressures are weighing on households.

items.title: Life-saving breast cancer and endometriosis drug to be pulled from shelves
items.description: Patients have been left frustrated and scared after learning that a life-saving breast cancer and endometriosis drug is to be pulled from shelves in Australia and some other countries.

items.title: Elderly NSW couple stabbed, alleged intruder shot during home invasion
items.description: A couple in their 70s have been critically injured and an alleged intruder has been shot during a suspected home invasion in northern NSW this morning.

items.title: Tour operators brace for Kakadu site closures 'like COVID all over again'
items.description: Parks Australia has announced popular Kakadu attractions Jim Jim Falls and Twin Falls will remain closed for the rest of the year, with one tourism operator saying the closures will lead to a "very hard" tourism season.

items.title: Ban on travelling under bridge being reviewed amid refuelling debacle
items.description: Authorities are considering whether it is feasible for Australia's Antarctic icebreaker to safely travel under Hobart's Tasman Bridge, as the Tasmanian government tries to resolve a costly refuelling saga.

items.title: Concerns raised as mining companies take local groundwater leaving towns 'vulnerable'
items.description: As a major miner seeks approval to extend its magnetite ore operations in regional Western Australia to 2048, shires are increasingly concerned about ensuring there's enough groundwater to go around.
